public_rationale: The firm part of the claim is 'no profit'. The revenue figure is hedged with 'maybe' and is not scored as a precise number. On profit, the evidence supports Zitron. OpenAI posted a $13.5 billion net loss on $4.3 billion of revenue in the first half of 2025, and about an $8 billion operating loss, per The Information and the FT as reported by The Register. Anthropic's IPO prospectus, as reported by Reuters, shows a $42 billion net loss on $4.6 billion of revenue in 2025, and an $8.1 billion operating loss even after excluding financing write-downs. These are the two leading generative AI model companies, and both lost heavily on both measures. Their combined reported revenue is well under $40 billion, which is consistent with a rough, hedged 'maybe $40 billion' ceiling for the sector.
limitations: Smaller AI companies and the AI units of profitable big tech firms were not assessed.
The figures come from press reports of private disclosures, not audited public filings.

our_interpretation: 'Maybe' marks the $40 billion figure as a tentative, rough estimate. It is not scored as a firm number. It is only checked loosely for being of a plausible order of magnitude.
The firm, scorable part is 'no profit': the generative AI companies he is discussing, most centrally OpenAI and Anthropic, were not making a profit.
Target period: calendar 2025, the year he was describing at the time of the August 2025 post. Profit is judged on reported net and operating results.

'These companies' is read as the generative AI model companies he discusses throughout the post (OpenAI, Anthropic and similar). It does not mean the diversified hyperscalers, which do not report separate AI profits.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Reported 2025 results show that OpenAI or Anthropic, or generative AI companies generally, were profitable.
